title: SaVe-TAG: LLM-based Interpolation for Long-Tailed Text-Attributed Graphs

problem.claim: Long-tailed graph data makes it difficult for GNNs to generalize across both head and tail classes.

gap.claim: Existing VRM approaches largely rely on embedding-space arithmetic and fail to capture rich semantics in text-attributed graphs.

contributions.claim: SaVe-TAG is a semantic-aware VRM framework that uses LLMs for text-level interpolation to generate on-manifold, boundary-enriching synthetic minority-class samples.
The method introduces confidence-based edge assignment using graph topology to filter noisy generations and preserve structural consistency.
The work provides theoretical justification for the proposed method.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present SaVe-TAG as a novel VRM framework for long-tailed text-attributed graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on benchmark datasets.
The authors report that SaVe-TAG consistently outperforms numeric interpolation and prior long-tailed node-classification baselines.
The authors state that source code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-tailed graph distributions hinder balanced GNN generalization.
Embedding-space interpolation does not capture the semantics of text-attributed graphs.
SaVe-TAG applies LLM-based text-level interpolation to create synthetic minority-class samples.
Confidence-based edge assignment uses topology to reduce noisy generations and maintain structural consistency.
The authors provide theoretical justification, report benchmark experiments, and emphasize combining semantic and structural signals.

source_observation.claim: Embedding-space interpolation may miss semantic information in text-attributed graphs.

interpretation.claim: Interpolation strategies should operate at a representation level that preserves the task-relevant modality.

application.claim: For imbalanced multimodal graph data, consider semantic-level sample generation alongside representation-level augmentation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when text-level interpolation is preferable across datasets or tasks.

source_observation.claim: The method uses graph topology to filter generated samples through confidence-based edge assignment.

interpretation.claim: Structural constraints can help control noise introduced by semantic generation.

application.claim: When augmenting graph data with generated content, use topology-aware consistency checks where available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the confidence threshold, edge-assignment procedure, or behavior on graphs with unreliable topology.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative gains.
The theoretical justification and its assumptions are not described.
The LLM, interpolation procedure, edge-assignment details, and computational requirements are unspecified.
